Music - Wikipedia — e Baroque era of music took place from 1600 to 1750, coinciding with the ﬂourishing of the Baroque artistic style in Europe. e
Music - Wikipedia — start of the Baroque era was marked by the penning of the ﬁrst operas. Polyphonic contrapuntal music (music with separate,
Music - Wikipedia — simultaneous melodic lines) remained important during this period. German Baroque composers wrote for small ensembles including
Music - Wikipedia — strings, brass, and woodwinds, as well as for choirs and keyboard instruments such as pipe organ, harpsichord, and clavichord.
Music - Wikipedia — Musical complexity increased during this time. Several major musical forms were created, some of them which persisted into later
Music - Wikipedia — periods, seeing further development. ese include the fugue, the invention, the sonata, and the concerto.[55] e late Baroque style
Music - Wikipedia — was polyphonically complex and richly ornamented. Important composers from the Baroque era include Johann Sebastian Bach
Music - Wikipedia — (Cello suites), George Frideric Handel (Messiah), Georg Philipp Telemann and Antonio Vivaldi (e Four Seasons).
Music - Wikipedia — e music of the Classical period (1730 to 1820) aimed to imitate what were seen as the key elements of the art and philosophy of
Music - Wikipedia — Ancient Greece and Rome: the ideals of balance, proportion and disciplined expression. (Note: the music from the Classical period
Music - Wikipedia — should not be confused with Classical music in general, a term which refers to Western art music from the 5th century to the 2000s,
Music - Wikipedia — which includes the Classical period as one of a number of periods). Music from the Classical period has a lighter,
Music - Wikipedia — clearer and considerably simpler texture than the Baroque music which preceded it. e main style was homophony,
Music - Wikipedia — [56] where a prominent melody and a subordinate chordal accompaniment part are clearly distinct. Classical
Music - Wikipedia — instrumental melodies tended to be almost voicelike and singable. New genres were developed, and the fortepiano,
Music - Wikipedia — the forerunner to the modern piano, replaced the Baroque era harpsichord and pipe organ as the main keyboard
Music - Wikipedia — instrument (though pipe organ continued to be used in sacred music, such as Masses).
Music - Wikipedia — Importance was given to instrumental music. It was dominated by further development of musical forms initially
Music - Wikipedia — deﬁned in the Baroque period: the sonata, the concerto, and the symphony. Other main kinds were the trio, string quartet, serenade and
Music - Wikipedia — divertimento. e sonata was the most important and developed form. Although Baroque composers also wrote sonatas, the Classical style of
Music - Wikipedia — sonata is completely distinct. All of the main instrumental forms of the Classical era, from string quartets to symphonies and concertos, were
Music - Wikipedia — based on the structure of the sonata. e instruments used chamber music and orchestra became more standardized. In place of the basso
Music - Wikipedia — continuo group of the Baroque era, which consisted of harpsichord, organ or lute along with a number of bass instruments selected at the
Music - Wikipedia — discretion of the group leader (e.g., viol, cello, theorbo, serpent), Classical chamber groups used speciﬁed, standardized instruments (e.g., a
Music - Wikipedia — string quartet would be performed by two violins, a viola and a cello). e practice of improvised chord-playing by the continuo keyboardist or
Music - Wikipedia — lute player, a hallmark of Baroque music, underwent a gradual decline between 1750 and 1800.[57]
Music - Wikipedia — One of the most important changes made in the Classical period was the development of public concerts. e aristocracy still played a
Music - Wikipedia — signiﬁcant role in the sponsorship of concerts and compositions, but it was now possible for composers to survive without being permanent
Music - Wikipedia — employees of queens or princes. e increasing popularity of classical music led to a growth in the number and types of orchestras. e expansion of orchestral concerts
Music - Wikipedia — necessitated the building of large public performance spaces. Symphonic music including symphonies, musical accompaniment to ballet and mixed vocal/instrumental
Music - Wikipedia — genres, such as opera and oratorio, became more popular.[58][59][60]

Music - Wikipedia — Romantic music (c. 1820 to 1900) from the 19th century had many elements in common with the Romantic styles in literature
Music - Wikipedia — and painting of the era. Romanticism was an artistic, literary, and intellectual movement was characterized by its emphasis
Music - Wikipedia — on emotion and individualism as well as gloriﬁcation of all the past and nature. Romantic music expanded beyond the rigid
Music - Wikipedia — styles and forms of the Classical era into more passionate, dramatic expressive pieces and songs. Romantic composers such as
Music - Wikipedia — Wagner and Brahms aempted to increase emotional expression and power in their music to describe deeper truths or
Music - Wikipedia — human feelings. With symphonic tone poems, composers tried to tell stories and evoke images or landscapes using
Music - Wikipedia — instrumental music. Some composers promoted nationalistic pride with patriotic orchestral music inspired by folk music. e
Music - Wikipedia — emotional and expressive qualities of music came to take precedence over tradition.[61]
Music - Wikipedia — Romantic composers grew in idiosyncrasy, and went further in the syncretism of exploring diﬀerent art-forms in a musical
Music - Wikipedia — context, (such as literature), history (historical ﬁgures and legends), or nature itself. Romantic love or longing was a prevalent
Music - Wikipedia — theme in many works composed during this period. In some cases, the formal structures from the classical period continued
Music - Wikipedia — to be used (e.g., the sonata form used in string quartets and symphonies), but these forms were expanded and altered. In
Music - Wikipedia — many cases, new approaches were explored for existing genres, forms, and functions. Also, new forms were created that were
Music - Wikipedia — deemed beer suited to the new subject maer. Composers continued to develop opera and ballet music, exploring new
Music - Wikipedia — styles and themes.[38]
Music - Wikipedia — In the years aer 1800, the music developed by Ludwig van Beethoven and Franz Schubert introduced a more dramatic,
Music - Wikipedia — expressive style. In Beethoven's case, short motifs, developed organically, came to replace melody as the most signiﬁcant
Music - Wikipedia — compositional unit (an example is the distinctive four note ﬁgure used in his Fih Symphony). Later Romantic composers
Music - Wikipedia — such as Pyotr Ilyich Tchaikovsky, Antonín Dvořák, and Gustav Mahler used more unusual chords and more dissonance to
Music - Wikipedia — create dramatic tension. ey generated complex and oen much longer musical works. During the late Romantic
Music - Wikipedia — period, composers explored dramatic chromatic alterations of tonality, such as extended chords and altered chords,
Music - Wikipedia — which created new sound "colors." e late 19th century saw a dramatic expansion in the size of the orchestra, and
Music - Wikipedia — the Industrial Revolution helped to create beer instruments, creating a more powerful sound. Public concerts
Music - Wikipedia — became an important part of well-to-do urban society. It also saw a new diversity in theatre music, including
Music - Wikipedia — operea, and musical comedy and other forms of musical theatre.[38]

Music - Wikipedia — "Composition" is the act or practice of creating a song, an instrumental music piece, a work with both singing and
Music - Wikipedia — instruments, or another type of music. In many cultures, including Western classical music, the act of composing also
Music - Wikipedia — includes the creation of music notation, such as a sheet music "score", which is then performed by the composer or by other
Music - Wikipedia — singers or musicians. In popular music and traditional music, the act of composing, which is typically called songwriting,
Music - Wikipedia — may involve the creation of a basic outline of the song, called the lead sheet, which sets out the melody, lyrics and chord
Music - Wikipedia — progression. In classical music, the composer typically orchestrates his or her own compositions, but in musical theatre and
Music - Wikipedia — in pop music, songwriters may hire an arranger to do the orchestration. In some cases, a songwriter may not use notation at
Music - Wikipedia — all, and instead, compose the song in her mind and then play or record it from memory. In jazz and popular music, notable
Music - Wikipedia — recordings by inﬂuential performers are given the weight that wrien scores play in classical music.[72][73]
Music - Wikipedia — Even when music is notated relatively precisely, as in classical music, there are many decisions that a performer has to make,
Music - Wikipedia — because notation does not specify all of the elements of music precisely. e process of deciding how to perform music that
Music - Wikipedia — has been previously composed and notated is termed "interpretation". Diﬀerent performers' interpretations of the same work
Music - Wikipedia — of music can vary widely, in terms of the tempos that are chosen and the playing or singing style or phrasing of the melodies.
Music - Wikipedia — Composers and songwriters who present their own music are interpreting their songs, just as much as those who perform
Music - Wikipedia — the music of others. e standard body of choices and techniques present at a given time and a given place is referred to as
Music - Wikipedia — performance practice, whereas interpretation is generally used to mean the individual choices of a performer.[74]
Music - Wikipedia — Although a musical composition oen uses musical notation and has a single author, this is not always the case. A work of
Music - Wikipedia — music can have multiple composers, which oen occurs in popular music when a band collaborates to write a song, or in
Music - Wikipedia — musical theatre, when one person writes the melodies, a second person writes the lyrics, and a third person orchestrates the
Music - Wikipedia — songs. In some styles of music, such as the blues, a composer/songwriter may create, perform and record new songs or pieces
Music - Wikipedia — without ever writing them down in music notation. A piece of music can also be composed with words, images, or computer
Music - Wikipedia — programs that explain or notate how the singer or musician should create musical sounds. Examples range from avant-garde
Music - Wikipedia — music that uses graphic notation, to text compositions such as Aus den sieben Tagen, to computer programs that select sounds
Music - Wikipedia — for musical pieces. Music that makes heavy use of randomness and chance is called aleatoric music,[75] and is associated with
Music - Wikipedia — contemporary composers active in the 20th century, such as John Cage, Morton Feldman, and Witold Lutosławski. A commonly known example of chance-based music
Music - Wikipedia — is the sound of wind chimes jingling in a breeze.
Music - Wikipedia — e study of composition has traditionally been dominated by examination of methods and practice of Western classical music, but the deﬁnition of composition is
Music - Wikipedia — broad enough to include the creation of popular music and traditional music songs and instrumental pieces as well as spontaneously improvised works like those of free
Music - Wikipedia — jazz performers and African percussionists such as Ewe drummers.

Music - Wikipedia — Performance is the physical expression of music, which occurs when a song is
Music - Wikipedia — sung or piano piece, guitar melody, symphony, drum beat or other musical part is
Music - Wikipedia — played. In classical music, a work is wrien in music notation by a composer and
Music - Wikipedia — then performed once the composer is satisﬁed with its structure and
Music - Wikipedia — instrumentation. However, as it gets performed, the interpretation of a song or
Music - Wikipedia — piece can evolve and change. In classical music, instrumental performers, singers
Music - Wikipedia — or conductors may gradually make changes to the phrasing or tempo of a piece. In
Music - Wikipedia — popular and traditional music, the performers have more freedom to make
Music - Wikipedia — changes to the form of a song or piece. As such, in popular and traditional music
Music - Wikipedia — styles, even when a band plays a cover song, they can make changes such as
Music - Wikipedia — adding a guitar solo or inserting an introduction.[76]
Music - Wikipedia — A performance can either be planned out and rehearsed (practiced)—which is the norm in classical music, jazz big bands, and
Music - Wikipedia — many popular music styles–or improvised over a chord progression (a sequence of chords), which is the norm in small jazz
Music - Wikipedia — and blues groups. Rehearsals of orchestras, concert bands and choirs are led by a conductor. Rock, blues and jazz bands are
Music - Wikipedia — usually led by the bandleader. A rehearsal is a structured repetition of a song or piece by the performers until it can be sung or
Music - Wikipedia — played correctly and, if it is a song or piece for more than one musician, until the parts are together from a rhythmic and tuning
Music - Wikipedia — perspective.
Music - Wikipedia — Many cultures have strong traditions of solo performance (in which one singer or instrumentalist performs), such as in Indian
Music - Wikipedia — classical music, and in the Western art-music tradition. Other cultures, such as in Bali, include strong traditions of group
Music - Wikipedia — performance. All cultures include a mixture of both, and performance may range from improvised solo playing to highly
Music - Wikipedia — planned and organized performances such as the modern classical concert, religious processions, classical music festivals or
Music - Wikipedia — music competitions. Chamber music, which is music for a small ensemble with only one or a few of each type of instrument, is
Music - Wikipedia — oen seen as more intimate than large symphonic works.[77]
Music - Wikipedia — Musical improvisation is the creation of spontaneous music, oen within (or based on) a pre-existing harmonic framework, chord progression, or riﬀs. Improvisers use
Music - Wikipedia — the notes of the chord, various scales that are associated with each chord, and chromatic ornaments and passing tones which may be neither chord tones nor from the
Music - Wikipedia — typical scales associated with a chord. Musical improvisation can be done with or without preparation. Improvisation is a major part of some types of music, such as
Music - Wikipedia — blues, jazz, and jazz fusion, in which instrumental performers improvise solos, melody lines, and accompaniment parts.[78]
Music - Wikipedia — In the Western art music tradition, improvisation was an important skill during the Baroque era and during the Classical era. In the Baroque era, performers improvised
Music - Wikipedia — ornaments, and basso continuo keyboard players improvised chord voicings based on ﬁgured bass notation. As well, the top soloists were expected to be able to
Music - Wikipedia — improvise pieces such as preludes. In the Classical era, solo performers and singers improvised virtuoso cadenzas during concerts.

Music - Wikipedia — century art music composers have increasingly included improvisation in their creative work. In Indian classical music, improvisation is a core component and an
Music - Wikipedia — essential criterion of performances.
Music - Wikipedia — Music is composed and performed for many purposes, ranging from aesthetic pleasure, religious or ceremonial purposes, or
Music - Wikipedia — as an entertainment product for the marketplace. When music was only available through sheet music scores, such as during
Music - Wikipedia — the Classical and Romantic eras, music lovers would buy the sheet music of their favourite pieces and songs so that they
Music - Wikipedia — could perform them at home on the piano. With the advent of the phonograph, records of popular songs, rather than sheet
Music - Wikipedia — music became the dominant way that music lovers would enjoy their favourite songs. With the advent of home tape
Music - Wikipedia — recorders in the 1980s and digital music in the 1990s, music lovers could make tapes or playlists of favourite songs and take
Music - Wikipedia — them with them on a portable cassee player or MP3 player. Some music lovers create mix tapes of favourite songs, which
Music - Wikipedia — serve as a "self-portrait, a gesture of friendship, prescription for an ideal party… [and] an environment consisting solely of
Music - Wikipedia — what is most ardently loved".[79]
Music - Wikipedia — Amateur musicians can compose or perform music for their own pleasure and derive income elsewhere. Professional
Music - Wikipedia — musicians are employed by institutions and organisations, including armed forces (in marching bands, concert bands and
Music - Wikipedia — popular music groups), religious institutions, symphony orchestras, broadcasting or ﬁlm production companies, and music schools. Professional musicians sometimes
Music - Wikipedia — work as freelancers or session musicians, seeking contracts and engagements in a variety of seings. ere are oen many links between amateur and professional
Music - Wikipedia — musicians. Beginning amateur musicians take lessons with professional musicians. In community seings, advanced amateur musicians perform with professional
Music - Wikipedia — musicians in a variety of ensembles such as community concert bands and community orchestras.
Music - Wikipedia — A distinction is oen made between music performed for a live audience and music that is performed in a studio so that it can be recorded and distributed through the
Music - Wikipedia — music retail system or the broadcasting system. However, there are also many cases where a live performance in front of an audience is also recorded and distributed.
Music - Wikipedia — Live concert recordings are popular in both classical music and in popular music forms such as rock, where illegally taped live concerts are prized by music lovers. In
Music - Wikipedia — the jam band scene, live, improvised jam sessions are preferred to studio recordings.[80]

Music - Wikipedia — Music notation typically means the wrien expression of music notes and rhythms on paper using symbols. When music is wrien down, the pitches and rhythm of the
Music - Wikipedia — music, such as the notes of a melody, are notated. Music notation oen provides instructions on how to perform the music. For example, the sheet music for a song may
Music - Wikipedia — state the song is a "slow blues" or a "fast swing", which indicates the tempo and the genre. To read notation, a person must have an understanding of music theory,
Music - Wikipedia — harmony and the performance practice associated with a particular song or piece's genre.
Music - Wikipedia — Wrien notation varies with the style and period of music. Nowadays, notated music is produced as sheet music or, for individuals with computer scorewriter programs,
Music - Wikipedia — as an image on a computer screen. In ancient times, music notation was put onto stone or clay tablets.[37] To perform music from notation, a singer or instrumentalist
Music - Wikipedia — requires an understanding of the rhythmic and pitch elements embodied in the symbols and the performance practice that is associated with a piece of music or genre.
Music - Wikipedia — In genres requiring musical improvisation, the performer oen plays from music where only the chord changes and form of the song are wrien, requiring the
Music - Wikipedia — performer to have a great understanding of the music's structure, harmony and the styles of a particular genre e.g., jazz or country music.
Music - Wikipedia — In Western art music, the most common types of wrien notation are scores, which include all the music parts of an ensemble piece, and parts, which are the music
Music - Wikipedia — notation for the individual performers or singers. In popular music, jazz, and blues, the standard musical notation is the lead sheet, which notates the melody, chords,
Music - Wikipedia — lyrics (if it is a vocal piece), and structure of the music. Fake books are also used in jazz; they may consist of lead sheets or simply chord charts, which permit rhythm
Music - Wikipedia — section members to improvise an accompaniment part to jazz songs. Scores and parts are also used in popular music and jazz, particularly in large ensembles such as
Music - Wikipedia — jazz "big bands." In popular music, guitarists and electric bass players oen read music notated in tablature (oen abbreviated as "tab"), which indicates the location of
Music - Wikipedia — the notes to be played on the instrument using a diagram of the guitar or bass ﬁngerboard. Tablature was used in the Baroque era to notate music for the lute, a
Music - Wikipedia — stringed, freed instrument.[81]
Music - Wikipedia — Many types of music, such as traditional blues and folk music were not wrien down in sheet music; instead, they were originally preserved in the memory of
Music - Wikipedia — performers, and the songs were handed down orally, from one musician or singer to another, or aurally, in which a performer learns a song "by ear". When the
Music - Wikipedia — composer of a song or piece is no longer known, this music is oen classiﬁed as "traditional" or as a "folk song". Diﬀerent musical traditions have diﬀerent aitudes
Music - Wikipedia — towards how and where to make changes to the original source material, from quite strict, to those that demand improvisation or modiﬁcation to the music. A culture's
Music - Wikipedia — history and stories may also be passed on by ear through song.[82]

Music - Wikipedia — Music has many diﬀerent fundamentals or elements. Depending on the deﬁnition of "element" being used, these can include pitch, beat or pulse, tempo, rhythm, melody,
Music - Wikipedia — harmony, texture, style, allocation of voices, timbre or color, dynamics, expression, articulation, form, and structure. e elements of music feature prominently in the
Music - Wikipedia — music curriculums of Australia, the UK, and the US. All three curriculums identify pitch, dynamics, timbre, and texture as elements, but the other identiﬁed elements of
Music - Wikipedia — music are far from universally agreed upon. Below is a list of the three oﬃcial versions of the "elements of music":
Music - Wikipedia — ▪ Australia: pitch, timbre, texture, dynamics and expression, rhythm, form and structure.[83]
Music - Wikipedia — ▪ UK: pitch, timbre, texture, dynamics, duration, tempo, structure.[84]
Music - Wikipedia — ▪ USA: pitch, timbre, texture, dynamics, rhythm, form, harmony, style/articulation.[85]
Music - Wikipedia — In relation to the UK curriculum, in 2013 the term: "appropriate musical notations" was added to their list of elements and the title of the list was changed from the
Music - Wikipedia — "elements of music" to the "inter-related dimensions of music". e inter-related dimensions of music are listed as: pitch, duration, dynamics, tempo, timbre, texture,
Music - Wikipedia — structure, and appropriate musical notations.[86]

Music - Wikipedia — "rudimentary elements of music" and the "perceptual elements of music".[n 4]
Music - Wikipedia — Pitch is an aspect of a sound that we can hear, reﬂecting whether one musical sound, note, or tone is "higher" or "lower" than another musical sound, note, or tone. We
Music - Wikipedia — can talk about the highness or lowness of pitch in the more general sense, such as the way a listener hears a piercingly high piccolo note or whistling tone as higher in
Music - Wikipedia — pitch than a deep thump of a bass drum. We also talk about pitch in the precise sense associated with musical melodies, basslines and chords. Precise pitch can only be
Music - Wikipedia — determined in sounds that have a frequency that is clear and stable enough to distinguish from noise. For example, it is much easier for listeners to discern the pitch of a
Music - Wikipedia — single note played on a piano than to try to discern the pitch of a crash cymbal that is struck.[91]

Music - Wikipedia — Harmony refers to the "vertical" sounds of pitches in music, which means pitches that are played or sung together at the
Music - Wikipedia — same time creates a chord. Usually, this means the notes are played at the same time, although harmony may also be implied
Music - Wikipedia — by a melody that outlines a harmonic structure (i.e., by using melody notes that are played one aer the other, outlining the
Music - Wikipedia — notes of a chord). In music wrien using the system of major-minor tonality ("keys"), which includes most classical music
Music - Wikipedia — wrien from 1600 to 1900 and most Western pop, rock, and traditional music, the key of a piece determines the "home note"
Music - Wikipedia — or tonic to which the piece generally resolves, and the character (e.g. major or minor) of the scale in use. Simple classical
Music - Wikipedia — pieces and many pop and traditional music songs are wrien so that all the music is in a single key. More complex Classical,
Music - Wikipedia — pop, and traditional music songs and pieces may have two keys (and in some cases three or more keys). Classical music from
Music - Wikipedia — the Romantic era (wrien from about 1820–1900) oen contains multiple keys,[93] as does jazz, especially Bebop jazz from the
Music - Wikipedia — 1940s, in which the key or "home note" of a song may change every four bars or even every two bars.[94]
Music - Wikipedia — Rhythm is the arrangement of sounds and silences in time. Meter animates time in regular pulse groupings, called measures
Music - Wikipedia — or bars, which in Western classical, popular, and traditional music oen group notes in sets of two (e.g., 2/4 time), three (e.g., 3/4 time, also known as Waltz time, or 3/8
Music - Wikipedia — time), or four (e.g., 4/4 time). Meters are made easier to hear because songs and pieces oen (but not always) place an emphasis on the ﬁrst beat of each grouping.
Music - Wikipedia — Notable exceptions exist, such as the backbeat used in much Western pop and rock, in which a song that uses a measure that consists of four beats (called 4/4 time or
Music - Wikipedia — common time) will have accents on beats two and four, which are typically performed by the drummer on the snare drum, a loud and distinctive-sounding percussion
Music - Wikipedia — instrument. In pop and rock, the rhythm parts of a song are played by the rhythm section, which includes chord-playing instruments (e.g., electric guitar, acoustic
Music - Wikipedia — guitar, piano, or other keyboard instruments), a bass instrument (typically electric bass or for some styles such as jazz and bluegrass, double bass) and a drum kit player.

Music - Wikipedia — ▪ monophony: a single melody (or "tune") with neither instrumental accompaniment nor a harmony part. A mother singing a lullaby to her baby
Music - Wikipedia — would be an example.
Music - Wikipedia — ▪ heterophony: two or more instruments or singers playing/singing the same melody, but with each performer slightly varying the rhythm or
Music - Wikipedia — speed of the melody or adding diﬀerent ornaments to the melody. Two bluegrass ﬁddlers playing the same traditional ﬁddle tune together will
Music - Wikipedia — typically each vary the melody by some degree and each add diﬀerent ornaments.
Music - Wikipedia — ▪ polyphony: multiple independent melody lines that interweave together, which are sung or played at the same time. Choral music written in the
Music - Wikipedia — Renaissance music era was typically written in this style. A round, which is a song such as "Row, Row, Row Your Boat", which diﬀerent groups of
Music - Wikipedia — singers all start to sing at a diﬀerent time, is an example of polyphony.
Music - Wikipedia — ▪ homophony: a clear melody supported by chordal accompaniment. Most Western popular music songs from the 19th century onward are
Music - Wikipedia — written in this texture.
Music - Wikipedia — Music that contains a large number of independent parts (e.g., a double concerto accompanied by 100 orchestral instruments with many interweaving melodic lines) is
Music - Wikipedia — generally said to have a "thicker" or "denser" texture than a work with few parts (e.g., a solo ﬂute melody accompanied by a single cello).
Music - Wikipedia — Timbre, sometimes called "color" or "tone color" is the quality or sound of a voice or instrument.[97] Timbre is what makes a
Music - Wikipedia — particular musical sound diﬀerent from another, even when they have the same pitch and loudness. For example, a 440 Hz A
Music - Wikipedia — note sounds diﬀerent when it is played on oboe, piano, violin, or electric guitar. Even if diﬀerent players of the same
Music - Wikipedia — instrument play the same note, their notes might sound diﬀerent due to diﬀerences in instrumental technique (e.g., diﬀerent
Music - Wikipedia — embouchures), diﬀerent types of accessories (e.g., mouthpieces for brass players, reeds for oboe and bassoon players) or
Music - Wikipedia — strings made out of diﬀerent materials for string players (e.g., gut strings versus steel strings). Even two instrumentalists
Music - Wikipedia — playing the same note on the same instrument (one aer the other) may sound diﬀerent due to diﬀerent ways of playing the
Music - Wikipedia — instrument (e.g., two string players might hold the bow diﬀerently).
Music - Wikipedia — e physical characteristics of sound that determine the perception of timbre include the spectrum, envelope, and overtones
Music - Wikipedia — of a note or musical sound. For electric instruments developed in the 20th century, such as electric guitar, electric bass and
Music - Wikipedia — electric piano, the performer can also change the tone by adjusting equalizer controls, tone controls on the instrument, and
Music - Wikipedia — by using electronic eﬀects units such as distortion pedals. e tone of the electric Hammond organ is controlled by adjusting
Music - Wikipedia — drawbars.

Music - Wikipedia — In music, form describes the overall structure or plan of a song or piece of music,[100] and it describes the
Music - Wikipedia — layout of a composition as divided into sections.[101] In the early 20th century, Tin Pan Alley songs and
Music - Wikipedia — Broadway musical songs were oen in AABA thirty-two-bar form, in which the A sections repeated the
Music - Wikipedia — same eight bar melody (with variation) and the B section provided a contrasting melody or harmony for
Music - Wikipedia — eight bars. From the 1960s onward, Western pop and rock songs are oen in verse-chorus form, which
Music - Wikipedia — comprises a sequence of verse and chorus ("refrain") sections, with new lyrics for most verses and
Music - Wikipedia — repeating lyrics for the choruses. Popular music oen makes use of strophic form, sometimes in
Music - Wikipedia — conjunction with the twelve bar blues.[102]
Music - Wikipedia — In the tenth edition of e Oxford Companion to Music, Percy Scholes deﬁnes musical form as "a series of
Music - Wikipedia — strategies designed to ﬁnd a successful mean between the opposite extremes of unrelieved repetition and
Music - Wikipedia — unrelieved alteration."[103] Examples of common forms of Western music include the fugue, the invention,
Music - Wikipedia — sonata-allegro, canon, strophic, theme and variations, and rondo.
Music - Wikipedia — Scholes states that European classical music had only six stand-alone forms: simple binary, simple
Music - Wikipedia — ternary, compound binary, rondo, air with variations, and fugue (although musicologist Alfred Mann
Music - Wikipedia — emphasized that the fugue is primarily a method of composition that has sometimes taken on certain
Music - Wikipedia — structural conventions.[104])
Music - Wikipedia — Where a piece cannot readily be broken into sectional units (though it might borrow some form from a poem, story or programme), it is said to be through-composed.
Music - Wikipedia — Such is oen the case with a fantasia, prelude, rhapsody, etude (or study), symphonic poem, Bagatelle, impromptu or similar composition.[105] Professor Charles Keil
Music - Wikipedia — classiﬁed forms and formal detail as "sectional, developmental, or variational."[106]

Music - Wikipedia — In ancient times, such as with the Ancient Greeks, the aesthetics of music explored the mathematical and cosmological dimensions of
Music - Wikipedia — rhythmic and harmonic organization. In the 18th century, focus shied to the experience of hearing music, and thus to questions
Music - Wikipedia — about its beauty and human enjoyment (plaisir and jouissance) of music. e origin of this philosophic shi is sometimes aributed to
Music - Wikipedia — Alexander Golieb Baumgarten in the 18th century, followed by Immanuel Kant. rough their writing, the ancient term 'aesthetics',
Music - Wikipedia — meaning sensory perception, received its present-day connotation. In the 2000s, philosophers have tended to emphasize issues besides
Music - Wikipedia — beauty and enjoyment. For example, music's capacity to express emotion has been foregrounded.[107]
Music - Wikipedia — In the 20th century, important contributions were made by Peter Kivy, Jerrold Levinson, Roger Scruton, and Stephen Davies. However,
Music - Wikipedia — many musicians, music critics, and other non-philosophers have contributed to the aesthetics of music. In the 19th century, a signiﬁcant debate arose between Eduard
Music - Wikipedia — Hanslick, a music critic and musicologist, and composer Richard Wagner regarding whether music can express meaning. Harry Partch and some other musicologists,
Music - Wikipedia — such as Kyle Gann, have studied and tried to popularize microtonal music and the usage of alternate musical scales. Modern composers like La Monte Young, Rhys
Music - Wikipedia — Chatham and Glenn Branca paid much aention to a scale called just intonation.[108][109][110]
Music - Wikipedia — It is oen thought that music has the ability to aﬀect our emotions, intellect, and psychology; it can assuage our loneliness or incite our passions. e philosopher Plato
Music - Wikipedia — suggests in e Republic that music has a direct eﬀect on the soul. erefore, he proposes that in the ideal regime music would be closely regulated by the state (Book
Music - Wikipedia — VII).[111] In Ancient China, the philosopher Confucius believed that music and rituals or rites are interconnected and harmonious with nature; he stated that music was
Music - Wikipedia — the harmonization of heaven and earth, while the order was brought by the rites order, making them extremely crucial functions in society.[112]

Music - Wikipedia — knowledge tends to advance on the basis of interpretations of data collected by systematic observation of and interaction with human participants. In addition to its
Music - Wikipedia — focus on fundamental perceptions and cognitive processes, music psychology is a ﬁeld of research with practical relevance for many areas, including music

Music - Wikipedia — Cognitive neuroscience of music is the scientiﬁc study of brain-based mechanisms involved in the cognitive processes
Music - Wikipedia — underlying music. ese behaviours include music listening, performing, composing, reading, writing, and ancillary
Music - Wikipedia — activities. It also is increasingly concerned with the brain basis for musical aesthetics and musical emotion. e ﬁeld is
Music - Wikipedia — distinguished by its reliance on direct observations of the brain, using such techniques as functional magnetic resonance
Music - Wikipedia — imaging (fMRI), transcranial magnetic stimulation (TMS), magnetoencephalography (MEG), electroencephalography (EEG),
Music - Wikipedia — and positron emission tomography (PET).
Music - Wikipedia — Cognitive musicology is a branch of cognitive science concerned with computationally modeling musical knowledge with the
Music - Wikipedia — goal of understanding both music and cognition.[114] e use of computer models provides an exacting, interactive medium
Music - Wikipedia — in which to formulate and test theories and has roots in artiﬁcial intelligence and cognitive science.[115]
Music - Wikipedia — Cognitive musicology investigates topics such as the parallels between language and music in the brain. Research oen includes biologically inspired models of
Music - Wikipedia — computation, such as neural networks and evolutionary programs.[116] is ﬁeld seeks to model how musical knowledge is represented, stored, perceived, performed,
Music - Wikipedia — and generated. By using a well-structured computer environment, the systematic structures of these cognitive phenomena can be investigated.[117]
Music - Wikipedia — Psychoacoustics is the scientiﬁc study of sound perception. More speciﬁcally, it is the branch of science studying the psychological and physiological responses
Music - Wikipedia — associated with sound (including speech and music). It can be further categorized as a branch of psychophysics.
Music - Wikipedia — Evolutionary musicology concerns the "origins of music, the question of animal song, selection pressures underlying music evolution", and "music evolution and human
Music - Wikipedia — evolution".[118] It seeks to understand music perception and activity in the context of evolutionary theory. Charles Darwin speculated that music may have held an
Music - Wikipedia — adaptive advantage and functioned as a protolanguage,[119] a view which has spawned several competing theories of music evolution.[120][121][122] An alternate view
Music - Wikipedia — sees music as a by-product of linguistic evolution; a type of "auditory cheesecake" that pleases the senses without providing any adaptive function.[123] is view has
Music - Wikipedia — been directly countered by numerous music researchers.[124][125][126]

Music - Wikipedia — Cultural eﬀects
Music - Wikipedia — biased toward culturally familiar musical traditions beginning in infancy, and adults' classiﬁcation of the emotion of a musical piece depends on both culturally speciﬁc
Music - Wikipedia — and universal structural features.[127][128] Additionally, individuals' musical memory abilities are greater for culturally familiar music than for culturally unfamiliar
Music - Wikipedia — music.[129][130]
Music - Wikipedia — Since the emergence of the study of psychoacoustics in the 1930s, most lists of elements of music have related more to how we hear music than how we learn to play it
Music - Wikipedia — or study it. C.E. Seashore, in his book Psychology of Music,[131] identiﬁed four "psychological aributes of sound". ese were: "pitch, loudness, time, and timbre" (p. 3).
Music - Wikipedia — He did not call them the "elements of music" but referred to them as "elemental components" (p. 2). Nonetheless, these elemental components link precisely with four of
Music - Wikipedia — the most common musical elements: "Pitch" and "timbre" match exactly, "loudness" links with dynamics, and "time" links with the time-based elements of rhythm,
Music - Wikipedia — duration, and tempo. is usage of the phrase "the elements of music" links more closely with Webster's New 20th Century Dictionary deﬁnition of an element as: "a
Music - Wikipedia — substance which cannot be divided into a simpler form by known methods"[132] and educational institutions' lists of elements generally align with this deﬁnition as well.
Music - Wikipedia — Although writers of lists of "rudimentary elements of music" can vary their lists depending on their personal (or institutional) priorities, the perceptual elements of
Music - Wikipedia — music should consist of an established (or proven) list of discrete elements which can be independently manipulated to achieve an intended musical eﬀect. It seems at
Music - Wikipedia — this stage that there is still research to be done in this area.
Music - Wikipedia — A slightly diﬀerent way of approaching the identiﬁcation of the elements of music, is to identify the "elements of sound" as: pitch, duration, loudness, timbre, sonic
Music - Wikipedia — texture and spatial location,[133] and then to deﬁne the "elements of music" as: sound, structure, and artistic intent.[133]

Music - Wikipedia — Ethnographic studies demonstrate that music is a participatory, community-based activity.[134][135] Music is experienced by individuals in a range of social seings from
Music - Wikipedia — being alone, to aending a large concert, forming a music community, which cannot be understood as a function of individual will or accident; it includes both
Music - Wikipedia — commercial and non-commercial participants with a shared set of common values. Musical performances take diﬀerent forms in diﬀerent cultures and socioeconomic
Music - Wikipedia — milieus.
Music - Wikipedia — In Europe and North America, there was a divide between what types of music were viewed as "high culture" and "low culture." "High culture" included Baroque,

Music - Wikipedia — Classical, Romantic, and modern-era symphonies, concertos, and solo works, and are typically heard in formal concerts in concert halls and churches, with the audience
Music - Wikipedia — siing quietly. Other types of music—including jazz, blues, soul, and country—are oen performed in bars, nightclubs, and theatres, where the audience may drink,
Music - Wikipedia — dance and cheer. Until the 20th century, the division between "high" and "low" musical forms was accepted as a valid distinction that separated out "art music", from
Music - Wikipedia — popular music heard in bars and dance halls. Musicologists, such as David Bracke, note a "redrawing of high-low cultural-aesthetic boundaries" in the 20th century.
Music - Wikipedia — [136] And, "when industry and public discourses link categories of music with categories of people, they tend to conﬂate stereotypes with actual listening
Music - Wikipedia — communities."[136] Stereotypes can be based on socioeconomic standing, or social class, of the performers or audience of the diﬀerent types of music.
Music - Wikipedia — When composers introduce styles of music that break with convention, there can be strong resistance from academics and others. Late-period Beethoven string
Music - Wikipedia — quartets, Stravinsky ballet scores, serialism, bebop, hip hop, punk rock, and electronica were controversial and criticised, when they were ﬁrst introduced. Such themes
Music - Wikipedia — are examined in the sociology of music, sometimes called sociomusicology, which is pursued in departments of sociology, media studies, or music, and is closely related
Music - Wikipedia — to ethnomusicology.
Music - Wikipedia — Women have played a major role in music throughout history, as composers, songwriters, instrumental performers, singers,
Music - Wikipedia — conductors, music scholars, music educators, music critics/music journalists and other musical professions. In the 2010s,
Music - Wikipedia — while women comprise a signiﬁcant proportion of popular music and classical music singers, and a signiﬁcant proportion of
Music - Wikipedia — songwriters (many of them being singer-songwriters), there are few women record producers, rock critics and rock
Music - Wikipedia — instrumentalists. Although there have been a huge number of women composers in classical music, from the medieval period
Music - Wikipedia — to the present day, women composers are signiﬁcantly underrepresented in the commonly performed classical music
Music - Wikipedia — repertoire, music history textbooks and music encyclopedias; for example, in the Concise Oxford History of Music, Clara
Music - Wikipedia — Schumann is one of the few female composers who is mentioned.
Music - Wikipedia — Women comprise a signiﬁcant proportion of instrumental soloists in classical music and the percentage of women in
Music - Wikipedia — orchestras is increasing. A 2015 article on concerto soloists in major Canadian orchestras, however, indicated that 84% of the
Music - Wikipedia — soloists with the Montreal Symphony Orchestra were men. In 2012, women still made up just 6% of the top-ranked Vienna
Music - Wikipedia — Philharmonic orchestra. Women are less common as instrumental players in popular music genres such as rock and heavy
Music - Wikipedia — metal, although there have been a number of notable female instrumentalists and all-female bands. Women are particularly
Music - Wikipedia — underrepresented in extreme metal genres.[137] In the 1960s pop-music scene, "[l]ike most aspects of the…music business, [in
Music - Wikipedia — the 1960s,] songwriting was a male-dominated ﬁeld. ough there were plenty of female singers on the radio, women …were
Music - Wikipedia — primarily seen as consumers:… Singing was sometimes an acceptable pastime for a girl, but playing an instrument, writing
Music - Wikipedia — songs, or producing records simply wasn't done."[138] Young women "…were not socialized to see themselves as people who
Music - Wikipedia — create [music]."[138]
Music - Wikipedia — Women are also underrepresented in orchestral conducting, music criticism/music journalism, music producing, and sound
Music - Wikipedia — engineering. While women were discouraged from composing in the 19th century, and there are few women musicologists, women became involved in music education
Music - Wikipedia — "…to such a degree that women dominated [this ﬁeld] during the later half of the 19th century and well into the 20th century."[139]

Music - Wikipedia — According to Jessica Duchen, a music writer for London's e Independent, women musicians in classical music are "…too oen judged for their appearances, rather than
Music - Wikipedia — their talent" and they face pressure "…to look sexy onstage and in photos."[140] Duchen states that while "[t]here are women musicians who refuse to play on their
Music - Wikipedia — looks,…the ones who do tend to be more materially successful."[140] According to the UK's Radio 3 editor, Edwina Wolstencro, the music industry has long been open
Music - Wikipedia — to having women in performance or entertainment roles, but women are much less likely to have positions of authority, such as being the conductor of an orchestra.[141]
Music - Wikipedia — In popular music, while there are many women singers recording songs, there are very few women behind the audio console acting as music producers, the individuals
Music - Wikipedia — who direct and manage the recording process.[142] One of the most recorded artists is Asha Bhosle, an Indian singer best known as a playback singer in Hindi cinema.

Music - Wikipedia — Since the 20th century, live music can be broadcast over the radio, television or the Internet, or recorded and listened to on a
Music - Wikipedia — CD player or MP3 player.
Music - Wikipedia — In the early 20th century (in the late 1920s), as talking pictures emerged in the early 20th century, with their prerecorded
Music - Wikipedia — musical tracks, an increasing number of moviehouse orchestra musicians found themselves out of work.[145] During the 1920s,
Music - Wikipedia — live musical performances by orchestras, pianists, and theater organists were common at ﬁrst-run theaters.[146] With the
Music - Wikipedia — coming of the talking motion pictures, those featured performances were largely eliminated. e American Federation of
Music - Wikipedia — Musicians (AFM) took out newspaper advertisements protesting the replacement of live musicians with mechanical playing
Music - Wikipedia — devices. One 1929 ad that appeared in the Pisburgh Press features an image of a can labeled "Canned Music / Big Noise Brand
Music - Wikipedia — / Guaranteed to Produce No Intellectual or Emotional Reaction Whatever"[147]
Music - Wikipedia — Sometimes, live performances incorporate prerecorded sounds. For example, a disc jockey uses disc records for scratching, and
Music - Wikipedia — some 20th-century works have a solo for an instrument or voice that is performed along with music that is prerecorded onto a
Music - Wikipedia — tape. Some pop bands use recorded backing tracks. Computers and many keyboards can be programmed to produce and play
Music - Wikipedia — Musical Instrument Digital Interface (MIDI) music. Audiences can also become performers by participating in karaoke, an
Music - Wikipedia — activity of Japanese origin centered on a device that plays voice-eliminated versions of well-known songs. Most karaoke
Music - Wikipedia — machines also have video screens that show lyrics to songs being performed; performers can follow the lyrics as they sing over
Music - Wikipedia — the instrumental tracks.
Music - Wikipedia — e advent of the Internet and widespread high-speed broadband access has transformed the experience of music, partly
Music - Wikipedia — through the increased ease of access to recordings of music via streaming video and vastly increased choice of music for
Music - Wikipedia — consumers. Another eﬀect of the Internet arose with online communities and social media websites like YouTube and
Music - Wikipedia — Facebook, a social networking service. ese sites make it easier for aspiring singers and amateur bands to distribute videos of
Music - Wikipedia — their songs, connect with other musicians, and gain audience interest. Professional musicians also use YouTube as a free publisher of promotional material. YouTube
Music - Wikipedia — users, for example, no longer only download and listen to MP3s, but also actively create their own. According to Don Tapsco and Anthony D. Williams, in their book
Music - Wikipedia — Wikinomics, there has been a shi from a traditional consumer role to what they call a "prosumer" role, a consumer who both creates content and consumes.

Music - Wikipedia — e incorporation of music into general education from preschool to post
Music - Wikipedia — secondary education, is common in North America and Europe. Involvement in
Music - Wikipedia — playing and singing music is thought to teach basic skills such as concentration,
Music - Wikipedia — counting, listening, and cooperation while also promoting understanding of
Music - Wikipedia — language, improving the ability to recall information, and creating an environment
Music - Wikipedia — more conducive to learning in other areas.[149] In elementary schools, children
Music - Wikipedia — oen learn to play instruments such as the recorder, sing in small choirs, and learn
Music - Wikipedia — about the history of Western art music and traditional music. Some elementary school children also learn about popular
Music - Wikipedia — music styles. In religious schools, children sing hymns and other religious music. In secondary schools (and less commonly in
Music - Wikipedia — elementary schools), students may have the opportunity to perform in some types of musical ensembles, such as choirs (a
Music - Wikipedia — group of singers), marching bands, concert bands, jazz bands, or orchestras. In some school systems, music lessons on how to
Music - Wikipedia — play instruments may be provided. Some students also take private music lessons aer school with a singing teacher or
Music - Wikipedia — instrument teacher. Amateur musicians typically learn basic musical rudiments (e.g., learning about musical notation for musical scales and rhythms) and beginner- to
Music - Wikipedia — intermediate-level singing or instrument-playing techniques.
Music - Wikipedia — At the university level, students in most arts and humanities programs can receive credit for taking a few music courses, which typically take the form of an overview
Music - Wikipedia — course on the history of music, or a music appreciation course that focuses on listening to music and learning about diﬀerent musical styles. In addition, most North
Music - Wikipedia — American and European universities have some types of musical ensembles that students in arts and humanities are able to participate in, such as choirs, marching
Music - Wikipedia — bands, concert bands, or orchestras. e study of Western art music is increasingly common outside of North America and Europe, such as the Indonesian Institute of
Music - Wikipedia — the Arts in Yogyakarta, Indonesia, or the classical music programs that are available in Asian countries such as South Korea, Japan, and China. At the same time,
Music - Wikipedia — Western universities and colleges are widening their curriculum to include music of non-Western cultures, such as the music of Africa or Bali (e.g. Gamelan music).
Music - Wikipedia — People aiming to become professional musicians, singers, composers, songwriters, music teachers and practitioners of other music-related professions such as music
Music - Wikipedia — history professors, sound engineers, and so on study in specialized post-secondary programs oﬀered by colleges, universities and music conservatories. Some
Music - Wikipedia — institutions that train individuals for careers in music oﬀer training in a wide range of professions, as is the case with many of the top U.S. universities, which oﬀer
Music - Wikipedia — degrees in music performance (including singing and playing instruments), music history, music theory, music composition, music education (for individuals aiming to
Music - Wikipedia — become elementary or high school music teachers) and, in some cases, conducting. On the other hand, some small colleges may only oﬀer training in a single profession
Music - Wikipedia — (e.g., sound recording).

Music - Wikipedia — While most university and conservatory music programs focus on training students in classical music, there are universities
Music - Wikipedia — and colleges that train musicians for careers as jazz or popular music musicians and composers, with notable U.S. examples
Music - Wikipedia — including the Manhaan School of Music and the Berklee College of Music. Two schools in Canada which oﬀer professional
Music - Wikipedia — jazz training are McGill University and Humber College. Individuals aiming at careers in some types of music, such as heavy
Music - Wikipedia — metal music, country music or blues are unlikely to become professionals by completing degrees or diplomas. Instead, they
Music - Wikipedia — typically learn about their style of music by singing or playing in bands (oen beginning in amateur bands, cover bands and
Music - Wikipedia — tribute bands), studying recordings on DVD and the Internet, and working with already-established professionals in their
Music - Wikipedia — style of music, either through informal mentoring or regular music lessons. Since the 2000s, the increasing popularity and
Music - Wikipedia — availability of Internet forums and YouTube "how-to" videos have enabled singers and musicians from metal, blues and
Music - Wikipedia — similar genres to improve their skills. Many pop, rock and country singers train informally with vocal coaches and voice
Music - Wikipedia — teachers.[150][151]
Music - Wikipedia — Musicology, the academic study of music, is studied in universities and music conservatories. e earliest deﬁnitions from the
Music - Wikipedia — 19th century deﬁned three sub-disciplines of musicology: systematic musicology, historical musicology, and comparative
Music - Wikipedia — musicology or ethnomusicology. In 2010-era scholarship, one is more likely to encounter a division into music theory, music history, and ethnomusicology. Research in
Music - Wikipedia — musicology has oen been enriched by cross-disciplinary work, for example in the ﬁeld of psychoacoustics. e study of music of non-Western cultures, and cultural
Music - Wikipedia — study of music, is called ethnomusicology. Students can pursue study of musicology, ethnomusicology, music history, and music theory through diﬀerent types of
Music - Wikipedia — degrees, including bachelor's, master's and PhD.[152][153][154]
Music - Wikipedia — Music theory is the study of music, generally in a highly technical manner outside of other disciplines. More broadly it refers to any study of music, usually related in
Music - Wikipedia — some form with compositional concerns, and may include mathematics, physics, and anthropology. What is most commonly taught in beginning music theory classes
Music - Wikipedia — are guidelines to write in the style of the common practice period, or tonal music. eory, even of music of the common practice period, may take other forms.[155]
Music - Wikipedia — Musical set theory is the application of mathematical set theory to music, ﬁrst applied to atonal music. Speculative music theory, contrasted with analytic music theory, is
Music - Wikipedia — devoted to the analysis and synthesis of music materials, for example tuning systems, generally as preparation for composition.[156]
Music - Wikipedia — Zoomusicology is the study of the music of non-human animals, or the musical aspects of sounds produced by non-human animals. As George Herzog (1941) asked, "do
Music - Wikipedia — animals have music?" François-Bernard Mâche's Musique, mythe, nature, ou les Dauphins d'Arion (1983), a study of "ornitho-musicology" using a technique of Nicolas

Music - Wikipedia — In the West, much of the history of music that is taught deals with the Western civilization's art music, known as classical
Music - Wikipedia — music. e history of music in non-Western cultures ("world music" or the ﬁeld of "ethnomusicology") is also taught in
Music - Wikipedia — Western universities. is includes the documented classical traditions of Asian countries outside the inﬂuence of Western
Music - Wikipedia — Europe, as well as the folk or indigenous music of various other cultures. Popular or folk styles of music in non-Western
Music - Wikipedia — countries varied from culture to culture, and period to period. Diﬀerent cultures emphasised diﬀerent instruments,
Music - Wikipedia — techniques, singing styles and uses for music. Music has been used for entertainment, ceremonies, rituals, religious purposes
Music - Wikipedia — and for practical and artistic communication. Non-Western music has also been used for propaganda purposes, as was the
Music - Wikipedia — case with Chinese opera during the Cultural Revolution.
Music - Wikipedia — ere is a host of music classiﬁcations for non-Western music, many of which are caught up in the argument over the
Music - Wikipedia — deﬁnition of music. Among the largest of these is the division between classical music (or "art" music), and popular music (or
Music - Wikipedia — commercial music – including non-Western styles of rock, country, and pop music-related styles). Some genres do not ﬁt
Music - Wikipedia — neatly into one of these "big two" classiﬁcations, (such as folk music, world music, or jazz-related music).
Music - Wikipedia — As world cultures have come into greater global contact, their indigenous musical styles have oen merged with other styles,
Music - Wikipedia — which produces new styles. For example, the United States bluegrass style contains elements from Anglo-Irish, Scoish, Irish,
Music - Wikipedia — German and African instrumental and vocal traditions, which were able to fuse in the United States' multi-ethnic "melting
Music - Wikipedia — pot" society. Some types of world music contain a mixture of non-Western indigenous styles with Western pop music
Music - Wikipedia — elements. Genres of music are determined as much by tradition and presentation as by the actual music. Some works, like
Music - Wikipedia — George Gershwin's Rhapsody in Blue, are claimed by both jazz and classical music, while Gershwin's Porgy and Bess and
Music - Wikipedia — Leonard Bernstein's West Side Story are claimed by both opera and the Broadway musical tradition. Many music festivals for
Music - Wikipedia — non-Western music, include bands and singers from a particular musical genre, such as world music.[158][159]
Music - Wikipedia — Indian music, for example, is one of the oldest and longest living types of music, and is still widely heard and performed in
Music - Wikipedia — South Asia, as well as internationally (especially since the 1960s). Indian music has mainly three forms of classical music, Hindustani, Carnatic, and Dhrupad styles. It
Music - Wikipedia — has also a large repertoire of styles, which involve only percussion music such as the talavadya performances famous in South India.
Music - Wikipedia — Music therapy is an interpersonal process in which a trained therapist uses music and all of its facets—physical, emotional, mental, social, aesthetic, and spiritual—to
Music - Wikipedia — Ethnomusicology
Music - Wikipedia — erapy
Music - Wikipedia — A music therapist from a "Blues in the
Music - Wikipedia — Schools" program plays harmonica
Music - Wikipedia — with a US Navy sailor at a Naval

Music - Wikipedia — help clients to improve or maintain their health. In some instances, the client's needs are addressed directly through music; in
Music - Wikipedia — others they are addressed through the relationships that develop between the client and therapist. Music therapy is used with
Music - Wikipedia — individuals of all ages and with a variety of conditions, including: psychiatric disorders, medical problems, physical
Music - Wikipedia — disabilities, sensory impairments, developmental disabilities, substance abuse issues, communication disorders, interpersonal
Music - Wikipedia — problems, and aging. It is also used to improve learning, build self-esteem, reduce stress, support physical exercise, and
Music - Wikipedia — facilitate a host of other health-related activities. Music therapists may encourage clients to sing, play instruments, create
Music - Wikipedia — songs, or do other musical activities.
Music - Wikipedia — In the 10th century, the philosopher Al-Farabi described how vocal music can stimulate the feelings and souls of listeners.
Music - Wikipedia — [160] Music has long been used to help people deal with their emotions. In the 17th century, the scholar Robert Burton's e
Music - Wikipedia — Anatomy of Melancholy argued that music and dance were critical in treating mental illness, especially melancholia.[161] He
Music - Wikipedia — noted that music has an "excellent power …to expel many other diseases" and he called it "a sovereign remedy against despair
Music - Wikipedia — and melancholy." He pointed out that in Antiquity, Canus, a Rhodian ﬁddler, used music to "make a melancholy man merry,
Music - Wikipedia — …a lover more enamoured, a religious man more devout."[162][163][164] In the Ooman Empire, mental illnesses were treated
Music - Wikipedia — with music.[165] In November 2006, Michael J. Crawford and his colleagues also found that music therapy helped schizophrenic patients.[166][167]

Imagination - Wikipedia — Imagination is the production of sensations, feelings and thoughts informing oneself.[1] ese experiences can be re-
Imagination - Wikipedia — creations of past experiences, such as vivid memories with imagined changes, or completely invented and possibly fantastic
Imagination - Wikipedia — scenes.[2] Imagination helps apply knowledge to solve problems and is fundamental to integrating experience and the
Imagination - Wikipedia — learning process.[3][4][5]
Imagination - Wikipedia — Imagination is the process of developing theories and ideas based on the functioning of the mind through a creative division.
Imagination - Wikipedia — Drawing from actual perceptions, imagination employs intricate conditional processes that engage both semantic and
Imagination - Wikipedia — episodic memory to generate new or reﬁned ideas.[6] is part of the mind helps develop beer and easier ways to
Imagination - Wikipedia — accomplish tasks, whether old or new.
Imagination - Wikipedia — A way to train imagination is by listening to and practicing storytelling (narrative),[3][7] wherein imagination is expressed
Imagination - Wikipedia — through stories and writings such as fairy tales, fantasies, and science ﬁction. When children develop their imagination, they
Imagination - Wikipedia — oen exercise it through pretend play. ey use role-playing to act out what they have imagined, and followingly, they play
Imagination - Wikipedia — on by acting as if their make-believe scenarios are actual reality.[8]
Imagination - Wikipedia — e English word "imagination" originates from the Latin term "imaginatio," which is the standard Latin translation of the
Imagination - Wikipedia — Greek term "phantasia." e Latin term also translates to "mental image" or "fancy." e use of the word "imagination" in
Imagination - Wikipedia — English can be traced back to the mid-14th century, referring to a faculty of the mind that forms and manipulates images.[9]
Imagination - Wikipedia — In modern philosophical understanding, imagination is commonly seen as a faculty for creating mental images and for
Imagination - Wikipedia — making non-rational, associative transitions among these images.[10]
Imagination - Wikipedia — One view of imagination links it to cognition, suggesting that imagination is a cognitive process in mental functioning.[11] It
Imagination - Wikipedia — is also associated with rational thinking in a way that both imaginative and rational thoughts involve the cognitive process
Imagination - Wikipedia — that "underpins thinking about possibilities".[12] However, imagination is not considered to be purely a cognitive activity
Imagination - Wikipedia — because it is also linked to the body and place. It involves seing up relationships with materials and people, precluding the

Imagination - Wikipedia — notion that imagination is conﬁned to the mind.[13]
Imagination - Wikipedia — e psychological view of imagination relates this concept to a cognate term, "mental imagery," which denotes the process of reviving in the mind recollections of
Imagination - Wikipedia — objects previously given in sense perception. Since this use of the term conﬂicts with that of ordinary language, some psychologists prefer to describe this process as
Imagination - Wikipedia — "imaging" or "imagery" or to speak of it as "reproductive" as opposed to "productive" or "constructive" imagination. Constructive imagination is further divided into
Imagination - Wikipedia — voluntary imagination driven by the lateral prefrontal cortex (LPFC), such as mental rotation, and involuntary imagination (LPFC-independent), such as REM sleep
Imagination - Wikipedia — dreaming, daydreaming, hallucinations, and spontaneous insight.[14] In clinical seings, clinicians nowadays increasingly make use of visual imagery for psychological
Imagination - Wikipedia — treatment of anxiety disorders, depression, schizophrenia and Parkinson's disease.[15]
Imagination - Wikipedia — Ancient Greek philosophers conceived imagination, or "phantasia," as working with "pictures" in the sense of mental images.[16] Aristotle, in his work De Anima,
Imagination - Wikipedia — identiﬁed imagination as a faculty that enables an image to occur within us,[17][18] a deﬁnition associating imagination with a broad range of activities involved in
Imagination - Wikipedia — thoughts, dreams, and memories.[18]
Imagination - Wikipedia — In Philebus, Plato discusses daydreaming and considers imagination about the future as the work of a painter within the soul.[19] However, Plato portrayed this painter
Imagination - Wikipedia — as an illustrator rather than a creator, reﬂecting his view of imagination as a representational rather than an inventive faculty.[20]
Imagination - Wikipedia — Greek philosophers typically distinguished imagination from perception and rational thinking: "For imagination is diﬀerent from either perceiving or discursive
Imagination - Wikipedia — thinking, though it is not found without sensation, or judgement without it" (De Anima, iii 3).[17][20]Aristotle viewed imagination as a faculty that mediates between the
Imagination - Wikipedia — senses and intellect.[18] e mental images it manipulates, whether arising from visions, dreams or sensory perception, were thought to be transmied through the
Imagination - Wikipedia — lower parts of the soul, suggesting that these images could be inﬂuenced by emotions and primal desires, thereby confusing the judgement of the intellect.[20]
Imagination - Wikipedia — In the Middle Ages, the concept of imagination encompassed domains such as religion, literature, artwork, and notably, poetry.[21] Men of science oen recognized poets
Imagination - Wikipedia — as "imaginative," viewing imagination as the mental faculty that speciﬁcally permied poetry writing.[22] is association, they suggested, lies in the capacity of
Imagination - Wikipedia — imagination for image-making and image-forming, which results in a sense of "visualizing" with "the inner eye."[16][23]
Imagination - Wikipedia — An epitome of this concept is Chaucer's idea of the "mind's eye" in e Man of Law's Tale from e Canterbury Tales (ca. 1390). He described a man who, although blind,
Imagination - Wikipedia — was able to "see" with an "eye of his mind":
Imagination - Wikipedia — "at oon of hem was blynd and myghte not see, / But it were with thilke eyen of his mynde / With whiche men seen, aer that they ben blynde."[24][25]
Imagination - Wikipedia — Conceptual history
Imagination - Wikipedia — Ancient
Imagination - Wikipedia — Middle Ages
Imagination - Wikipedia — Medieval paintings of imaginary
Imagination - Wikipedia — creatures, as seen in frescos and
Imagination - Wikipedia — manuscripts, often combined body
Imagination - Wikipedia — parts of diﬀerent animals, and even
Imagination - Wikipedia — humans.
Imagination - Wikipedia — Medieval theories of faculty psychology posited imagination as a faculty of the internal senses (alongside memory and common sense): imagination receives mental
Imagination - Wikipedia — images from memory or perception, organizes them, and transmits them to the reasoning faculties, providing the intellect with sense data.[26][27] In this way, it enables
Imagination - Wikipedia — the reshaping of images from sense perception (even in the absence of perception, such as in dreams), performing a ﬁltering function of reality.[22][28]
Imagination - Wikipedia — Although not aributed the capacity for creations, imagination was thought to combine images received from memory or
Imagination - Wikipedia — perception in creative ways, allowing for the invention of novel concepts or expressions.[27] For example, it could fuse images
Imagination - Wikipedia — of "gold" and "mountain" to produce the idea of a "golden mountain."[29]
Imagination - Wikipedia — In medieval artistic works, imagination served the role of combining images of perceivable things to portray legendary,
Imagination - Wikipedia — mysterious, or extraordinary creatures.[30] is can be seen in the depiction of a Mongolian in the Grandes Chroniques de
Imagination - Wikipedia — France(1241), as well as in the portrayal of angels, demons, hell, and the apocalypse in Christian religious paintings.[20][21]
Imagination - Wikipedia — e Renaissance saw the revival of classical texts and the celebration for men's dignity, yet scholars of the time did not
Imagination - Wikipedia — signiﬁcantly contribute to the conceptual understanding of "imagination."[16][26] Marsilio Ficino, for example, did not regard
Imagination - Wikipedia — artistic creations such as painting, sculpture and poetry as privileged forms of human creativity, nor did he aribute
Imagination - Wikipedia — creativity to the faculty of imagination. Instead, Ficino posited that imagination could be the vehicle through which divine
Imagination - Wikipedia — intervention transmits insights in the form of images, which ultimately facilitates the creation of art.[20][22][31]
Imagination - Wikipedia — Nevertheless, the groundwork laid by humanists made it easier for later thinkers to develop the connection between imagination and creativity.[20] Early modern
Imagination - Wikipedia — philosophers began to consider imagination as a trait or ability that an individual could possess. Miguel de Cervantes, inﬂuenced by Spanish physician and philosopher
Imagination - Wikipedia — Juan Huarte de San Juan, craed the iconic character Don ixote, who epitomized Huarte's idea of "wits full of invention."[28][32][33] is type of wit was thought to be
Imagination - Wikipedia — typically found in individuals for whom imagination was the most prominent component of their "ingenium" (Spanish: ingenio; term meaning close to "intellect").[34][28]
Imagination - Wikipedia — [35][36]
Imagination - Wikipedia — Early modern philosophers also started to acknowledge imagination as an active, cognitive faculty, although it was principally seen as a mediator between sense
Imagination - Wikipedia — perception (Latin: sensus) and pure understanding (Latin: intellectio pura).[16] René Descartes, in Meditations on First Philosophy (1641), interpreted imagination as a
Imagination - Wikipedia — faculty actively focusing on bodies (corporeal entities) while being passively dependent on stimuli from diﬀerent senses.[16][37][38] In the writing of omas Hobbes,
Imagination - Wikipedia — imagination became a key element of human cognition.[39]
Imagination - Wikipedia — In the 16th and 17th centuries, the connotations of imagination" extended to many areas of early modern civic life.[40][41] Juan Luis Vives noted the connection between
Imagination - Wikipedia — imagination and rhetoric skills.[42] Huarte extended this idea, linking imagination to any disciplines that necessitates "ﬁgures, correspondence, harmony, and
Imagination - Wikipedia — proportion," such as medical practice and the art of warfare.[34][43][44] Additionally, Galileo used the concept of imagination to conduct thought experiments, such as
Imagination - Wikipedia — asking readers to imagine the direction a stone released from a sling would ﬂy.[45]
